facts.text: Did you know Amsterdam is named after a dam? Its old name, Amestelledamme, means "dam in the Amstel", and it first shows up in a document from 1275.
Did you know Amsterdam's Royal Palace stands on 13,659 wooden poles, driven deep into the swampy ground in the 1600s?
facts.label: Royal Palace
facts.photo: File:Palacio Real, Ámsterdam, Países Bajos, 2016-05-30, DD 07-09 HDR.jpg

facts.text: The city has more than 100 kilometres of canals and about 1,500 bridges, and its 17th-century canal ring is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.label: Herengracht
facts.photo: File:Herengracht, Amsterdam in the Blue Hour.jpg

facts.text: Behind a moving bookcase at Prinsengracht 263, Anne Frank and seven others hid for more than two years during the Second World War.
facts.label: Anne Frank House

facts.text: Vondelpark opened in 1865 on old marshland, and today around 10 million people visit it every year.
facts.label: Vondelpark

facts.text: And under the water in front of Central Station, there's a garage for about 7,000 bicycles!
facts.label: Underwater bike garage

end.text: Which one surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments!

4. The Anne Frank House at Prinsengracht 263
